Case Description & Question:
A 55-year-old African American male presents for routine prostate cancer screening. His PSA level is 4.8 ng/mL, and his DRE findings are normal. He has a positive family history of prostate cancer in his father.  
What is the most appropriate next step in his management?
Answer Choices:
A) Repeat PSA in 6 months.  
B) Perform a prostate MRI.  
C) Proceed with a prostate biopsy.  
D) Start treatment with finasteride.  
E) Discontinue any further screening.
Correct Answer: C) Proceed with a prostate biopsy.
